title: Spiking World-Action Models for Robotic Manipulation
abstract: arXiv:2611.30041v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: World action models (WAMs) predict how the world responds to actions and offer a promising path toward general embodied intelligence, but they are large and run the network many times per plan, so they are hard to deploy on robots. Spiking neural networks (SNNs) compute with sparse binary spikes and use additions instead of multiplications, which saves power. However, existing WAMs use dense videos as the world state, so a spiking version would spend most of its computation on the background. We therefore introduce SpikingWAM, the first spiking WAM, which uses a sparse task skeleton as the world state. Inspired by biological motor control, which attends only to the key positions of a task, the Task Skeleton State (TSS) keeps the keypoints of the arm and the task objects, and a small spiking front end estimates the object keypoints from images. Body Frame Spike Coding (BFSC) and Grid Coincidence Attention (GCA) keep millimetre precision

translated_title: 面向机器人操作的脉冲世界-动作模型
translated_abstract: 世界-动作模型预测世界如何响应动作，为实现通用具身智能提供了一条有前景的路径，但这类模型体量庞大且每次规划需要多次运行网络，因此难以部署到机器人上。脉冲神经网络使用稀疏的二值脉冲进行计算，并用加法代替乘法，从而节省功耗。然而，现有的世界-动作模型使用密集视频作为世界状态，因此其脉冲化版本会把大部分计算浪费在背景上。为此，我们提出了SpikingWAM——首个脉冲世界-动作模型，它使用稀疏的任务骨架作为世界状态。受生物运动控制只关注任务关键位置的启发，任务骨架状态保留机械臂和任务物体的关键点，并由一个小型脉冲前端从图像中估计物体关键点。机体坐标系脉冲编码（BFSC）和网格重合注意力（GCA）则保持了毫米级的精度。
tldr: 提出了首个脉冲世界-动作模型SpikingWAM，通过任务骨架状态、机体坐标系脉冲编码和网格重合注意力，在保持毫米级操作精度的同时大幅降低计算量与功耗，使世界-动作模型能够高效部署到机器人上。
en_tdlr: SpikingWAM, the first spiking world-action model, leverages a sparse Task Skeleton State, Body Frame Spike Coding, and Grid Coincidence Attention to achieve millimeter-precision robotic manipulation while drastically reducing computation and power consumption.
